sentences.text: The Commission of Inquiry into Forensic DNA Testing in Queensland assessed whether DNA collection, testing and analysis met best practice and why any failures occurred.
sentences.support: whether the methods, systems and processes used in the collection, testing and analysis of DNA samples in Queensland were consistent with best practice

sentences.text: It examined laboratory practices, sample collection by police and medical practitioners, management and workplace culture.
sentences.support: the Queensland Police Service who collect samples at crimes scenes and from people, and medical professionals within Queensland Health who collect samples in cases of sexual assault

sentences.text: The Commission found that the laboratory prioritised processing speed over scientific quality and had failed to obtain available evidence in some cases.
sentences.support: The laboratory has, for some time, focused on throughput and quick reporting of results to the detriment of high-quality science.

sentences.text: The Commission found that the identified failures did not undermine the reliability of matches between crime scene DNA and reference samples, while the number of affected cases could not be quantified.
sentences.support: None of the failures I have identified call into question the reliability of a match

sentences.text: The Commission made 123 recommendations covering scientific procedures, review of past cases, governance and funding, including an independent forensic science institute within the Department of Justice and Attorney-General.
sentences.support: The creation of the institute as an independent office within the Department of Justice and Attorney-General

findings.quote: The laboratory has, for some time, focused on throughput and quick reporting of results to the detriment of high-quality science.

None of the failures I have identified call into question the reliability of a match between a crime scene sample and a person’s reference sample, the most probative evidence which often supports convictions.
Cultural issues have had a negative impact on the scientific processes used and the results obtained.

notes: The executive summary says over 100 recommendations; the report contains 123 consecutively numbered recommendations (Rec 1 to Rec 123). The summary preserves the distinction between failure to obtain available evidence and the reliability of DNA matches. The terms-of-reference appendix on PDF page 519 has garbled OCR; the executive summary and cited substantive sections are readable.
